title: Apostle Paul IQ
subtitle: From persecutor to apostle. How much do you know about the man who wrote half the New Testament?

questions.text: What was the apostle Paul's name before his conversion?

options.explanation: Simon was Peter's earlier name, not Paul's.
He was known as Saul of Tarsus before the Lord met him (Acts 9:1-4).
Silas was one of Paul's traveling companions, a different man.
Stephen was the first martyr, killed while Saul looked on.

questions.text: What was Paul doing to the early church before he became a believer?

options.explanation: Paul did not ignore the church. He actively hunted believers down.
Acts 8:3 says Saul made havoc of the church, dragging men and women off to prison.
Paul was no secret supporter. He was one of the church's fiercest enemies.
He became a leader only after his conversion, not before.

questions.text: Where was Paul headed when he met the risen Jesus in a blinding light?

options.explanation: Paul was leaving Jerusalem to hunt believers in another city when it happened.
Paul reached Rome much later, near the end of his life, not at his conversion.
Acts 9:3 says it happened as he neared Damascus, where he meant to arrest believers.
Antioch was a base for Paul's later missions, not the road of his conversion.

questions.text: What happened to Paul right after he saw the light on the road?

options.text: He was struck blind for three days
options.explanation: Acts 9:9 says he could not see for three days, until Ananias came and his sight returned.

options.text: He fell into a deep sleep
options.explanation: He did not fall asleep. He was left blind for three days.
Paul could still speak. It was his sight that he lost for a time.
He remembered the encounter clearly. What he lost was his sight, not his memory.

questions.text: What trade did Paul work with his own hands to support himself?

options.explanation: Fishing was the trade of Peter, James, and John, not Paul.
Acts 18:3 says Paul was a tentmaker by trade and worked alongside Aquila and Priscilla.
Carpentry was the trade of Jesus and Joseph, not Paul.
Paul used farming as an illustration at times, but his trade was making tents.

questions.text: Who was the young man Paul mentored and called his son in the faith?

options.explanation: Barnabas was Paul's partner and a leader in his own right, not his protege.
Paul called Timothy his own son in the faith and wrote two letters to him.
Luke was a doctor and traveling companion who wrote a Gospel and Acts.
Apollos was a gifted preacher who worked alongside Paul, but not the one he raised up as a son.

questions.text: Which of these letters in the New Testament did Paul write?

options.explanation: The letter of James was written by James, not Paul.
Romans is one of Paul's longest and most well-known letters, written to the church in Rome.
First Peter came from the apostle Peter, not Paul.
Jude was written by Jude, a brother of James, not by Paul.

questions.text: Paul wrote, "I can do all things in him that strengtheneth me." Which letter is that from?

options.explanation: Galatians deals mostly with grace and the law, not this verse.
That line is Philippians 4:13 (ASV), written while Paul was content even in hardship.
Ephesians is rich with teaching, but this verse comes from Philippians.
Colossians is a close companion letter, yet this particular verse is in Philippians.

questions.text: What hardship did Paul describe as a thorn in the flesh?

options.text: A debt he could not repay
options.explanation: The thorn was not about money. It was a personal trouble he asked God to remove.

options.text: A persistent affliction he pleaded with God to take away
options.explanation: In 2 Corinthians 12:7-9 Paul calls it a thorn in the flesh and says God's grace was sufficient for him.
Paul faced opponents, but the thorn in the flesh was an affliction, not a person.
The thorn had nothing to do with writings. It was a lasting affliction.

questions.text: Paul faced many dangers on his journeys. Which of these did he go through?

options.explanation: Acts 27 records a violent storm and shipwreck on Paul's voyage toward Rome.
Paul was never thrown to lions. He did, however, survive a shipwreck.
That was not part of Paul's story. He endured a shipwreck instead.
Paul did not drown. He survived the shipwreck on his way to Rome.

questions.text: As a Roman citizen on trial, what did Paul do to take his case to the emperor?

options.explanation: Paul did not offer a bribe. He used his legal right as a citizen.
In Acts 25:11 Paul says, "I appeal unto Caesar," using his right as a Roman citizen.
Paul did not flee. He appealed to Caesar to be heard in Rome.
Paul spoke for himself and appealed to Caesar rather than hiring a lawyer.

questions.text: On Paul's first missionary journey, who traveled with him as his main companion?

options.explanation: Acts 13:2-4 shows Barnabas set apart with Saul to begin the first missionary journey together.
Peter ministered mostly to Jewish believers and was not Paul's companion on this trip.
John the Baptist had died before Paul's missions began.
Matthew wrote a Gospel but did not travel with Paul on this journey.

scoring.perfectMessage: Perfect. You know Paul's story from Damascus to Rome.

gradeBands.label: Just Meeting Paul
gradeBands.message: Paul's life is one of the great stories of the Bible. Read on.

gradeBands.label: Getting Acquainted
gradeBands.message: You know the main beats of Paul's life. Keep going.

gradeBands.label: Fellow Traveler
gradeBands.message: You know Paul's journey well. Nicely done.

gradeBands.label: Paul Scholar
gradeBands.message: From persecutor to apostle, you know it all.
